findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) in test_basic is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched away
findings.body: test_basic starts with `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which patches the `sleep` attribute on the `time` module globally. The newly added lines `step.poll(); time.sleep(0.1)` (with the comment "Give flusher threads time to process after drift change") therefore call the no-op lambda — the test does not actually wait for the flusher thread to observe the drift change and flush. Whether the flush happens before `step.join()` depends on thread scheduling, making this test flaky: on a slow or loaded CI runner the flusher thread may not have produced the message yet, and `(msg,) = messages` will fail intermittently. Use a real wait (e.g., a threading.Event, polling loop with a deadline, or `time.sleep` from an unpatched reference saved before monkeypatching) instead.

findings.title: max_processes=0 silently becomes one process per shard
findings.body: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats any falsy value as 'unset'. The new `--flusher-processes` CLI option accepts any integer, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` (or a negative number, which is also not validated) results in spawning one flusher process per shard instead of being rejected — the opposite of what an operator might intend when trying to disable extra flusher processes. Consider validating the click option (`type=click.IntRange(min=1)`) or checking `max_processes is None` explicitly instead of using truthiness.
